# ANY CHEAPEST selects, for each pair of endpoints, a path whose edge COST values sum lowest.
# third_party/bigquery_docs/reference/standard-sql/graph-patterns.md
# TransferGraph edges: 7->16 (300), 7->16 (100), 16->20 (300), 20->7 (500), 20->16 (200).
# Never assert which path is chosen when several paths cost the same.

# The documented example, with its table as written.
SELECT STRING_AGG(FORMAT('%d:%d:%d', a_id, b_id, total_cost), ',' ORDER BY a_id, b_id) FROM GRAPH_TABLE(scalar_graph.TransferGraph MATCH ANY CHEAPEST (a:Account)-[t:Transfers COST t.amount]->{1,3}(b:Account) LET total_cost = sum(t.amount) RETURN a.id AS a_id, b.id AS b_id, total_cost)
=> "7:7:900,7:16:100,7:20:400,16:7:800,16:16:500,16:20:300,20:7:500,20:16:200,20:20:500"

# The cheapest path can have more edges than the shortest: 20->7->16 costs 600, the direct
# edge 1000.
SELECT result FROM GRAPH_TABLE(scalar_graph.TransferGraph MATCH ANY CHEAPEST (a:Account WHERE a.id = 20)-[e:Transfers COST IF(e.amount = 200, 1000, e.amount)]->{1,2}(b:Account WHERE b.id = 16) RETURN ARRAY_LENGTH(e) AS result)
=> "2"

# Costs of a composed path add across its parts; edges without COST add nothing.
SELECT STRING_AGG(FORMAT('%d:%d:%d', d, hops, first), ',' ORDER BY d) FROM GRAPH_TABLE(scalar_graph.TransferGraph MATCH ANY CHEAPEST (a:Account WHERE a.id = 7)-[e1:Transfers COST e1.amount]->{1,2}(b:Account WHERE b.id = 20)-[e2:Transfers]->(-[e3:Transfers COST e3.amount * 10]->){1,2}(c:Account) RETURN c.id AS d, ARRAY_LENGTH(e3) AS hops, e3[OFFSET(0)].amount AS first)
=> "7:2:300,16:1:100,20:1:300"

# A zero-edge path costs nothing, so it wins for identical endpoints.
SELECT result FROM GRAPH_TABLE(scalar_graph.TransferGraph MATCH p = ANY CHEAPEST (a:Account)-[e:Transfers COST e.amount]->{0,2}(b:Account) RETURN SUM(PATH_LENGTH(p)) AS result)
=> "8"

# Without ANY CHEAPEST, COST selects nothing, and BigQuery does not check it: a zero cost
# matches, as observed with tools/bqanswers.
SELECT result FROM GRAPH_TABLE(scalar_graph.TransferGraph MATCH (a:Account)-[e:Transfers COST e.amount]->(b:Account) RETURN COUNT(*) AS result)
=> "5"
SELECT result FROM GRAPH_TABLE(scalar_graph.TransferGraph MATCH (a:Account)-[e:Transfers COST e.amount - 100]->(b:Account) RETURN COUNT(*) AS result)
=> "5"

# Where the result depends on the selected path, a NULL, zero, negative, infinite or NaN cost is
# a runtime error, as documented in
# third_party/bigquery_docs/reference/standard-sql/graph-patterns.md, with these messages, and so
# is a total that overflows its type; observed BigQuery answers collected with tools/bqanswers.
# BigQuery answered COUNT(*) of the same paths without an error; see known_bugs.txt.
SELECT STRING_AGG(FORMAT('%d:%d:%d', a_id, b_id, amount), ',' ORDER BY a_id, b_id) FROM GRAPH_TABLE(scalar_graph.TransferGraph MATCH ANY CHEAPEST (a:Account)-[e:Transfers COST e.amount]->(b:Account) RETURN a.id AS a_id, b.id AS b_id, e.amount AS amount)
=> "7:16:100,16:20:300,20:7:500,20:16:200"
SELECT STRING_AGG(FORMAT('%d:%d:%d', a_id, b_id, amount), ',' ORDER BY a_id, b_id) FROM GRAPH_TABLE(scalar_graph.TransferGraph MATCH ANY CHEAPEST (a:Account)-[e:Transfers COST IF(e.amount = 100, NULL, e.amount)]->(b:Account) RETURN a.id AS a_id, b.id AS b_id, e.amount AS amount)
=> error contains: Graph cost expression must not be NULL
SELECT STRING_AGG(FORMAT('%d:%d:%d', a_id, b_id, amount), ',' ORDER BY a_id, b_id) FROM GRAPH_TABLE(scalar_graph.TransferGraph MATCH ANY CHEAPEST (a:Account)-[e:Transfers COST IF(e.amount > 0, NULL, e.amount)]->(b:Account) RETURN a.id AS a_id, b.id AS b_id, e.amount AS amount)
=> error contains: Graph cost expression must not be NULL
SELECT STRING_AGG(FORMAT('%d:%d:%d', a_id, b_id, amount), ',' ORDER BY a_id, b_id) FROM GRAPH_TABLE(scalar_graph.TransferGraph MATCH ANY CHEAPEST (a:Account)-[e:Transfers COST e.amount - 100]->(b:Account) RETURN a.id AS a_id, b.id AS b_id, e.amount AS amount)
=> error contains: Graph cost expression must be positive
SELECT STRING_AGG(FORMAT('%d:%d:%d', a_id, b_id, amount), ',' ORDER BY a_id, b_id) FROM GRAPH_TABLE(scalar_graph.TransferGraph MATCH ANY CHEAPEST (a:Account)-[e:Transfers COST IF(e.amount = 300, -1, e.amount)]->(b:Account) RETURN a.id AS a_id, b.id AS b_id, e.amount AS amount)
=> error contains: Graph cost expression must be positive
SELECT STRING_AGG(FORMAT('%d:%d:%d', a_id, b_id, amount), ',' ORDER BY a_id, b_id) FROM GRAPH_TABLE(scalar_graph.TransferGraph MATCH ANY CHEAPEST (a:Account)-[e:Transfers COST IF(e.amount = 100, IEEE_DIVIDE(1, 0), e.amount)]->(b:Account) RETURN a.id AS a_id, b.id AS b_id, e.amount AS amount)
=> error contains: Graph cost expression must not be Inf
SELECT STRING_AGG(FORMAT('%d:%d:%d', a_id, b_id, amount), ',' ORDER BY a_id, b_id) FROM GRAPH_TABLE(scalar_graph.TransferGraph MATCH ANY CHEAPEST (a:Account)-[e:Transfers COST IF(e.amount = 100, IEEE_DIVIDE(0, 0), e.amount)]->(b:Account) RETURN a.id AS a_id, b.id AS b_id, e.amount AS amount)
=> error contains: Graph cost expression must not be NaN
# BigQuery's message is "int64 overflow: 9223372036854775507 + 9223372036854775507".
SELECT STRING_AGG(FORMAT('%d:%d:%d', a_id, c_id, amount), ',' ORDER BY a_id, c_id) FROM GRAPH_TABLE(scalar_graph.TransferGraph MATCH ANY CHEAPEST (a:Account)-[e1:Transfers COST 9223372036854775807 - e1.amount]->(b:Account)-[e2:Transfers COST 9223372036854775807 - e2.amount]->(c:Account) RETURN a.id AS a_id, c.id AS c_id, e1.amount + e2.amount AS amount)
=> error:

# ANY CHEAPEST needs a COST, on every quantified edge pattern, of a numeric type, and only on
# edge patterns.
SELECT result FROM GRAPH_TABLE(scalar_graph.TransferGraph MATCH ANY CHEAPEST (a:Account)-[e:Transfers]->{1,2}(b:Account) RETURN COUNT(*) AS result)
=> error:
SELECT result FROM GRAPH_TABLE(scalar_graph.TransferGraph MATCH ANY CHEAPEST (a:Account)-[e1:Transfers COST e1.amount]->(b:Account)-[e2:Transfers]->{1,2}(c:Account) RETURN COUNT(*) AS result)
=> error:
SELECT result FROM GRAPH_TABLE(scalar_graph.TransferGraph MATCH ANY CHEAPEST (a:Account)-[e:Transfers COST CAST(e.amount AS STRING)]->(b:Account) RETURN COUNT(*) AS result)
=> error:
SELECT result FROM GRAPH_TABLE(scalar_graph.TransferGraph MATCH ANY CHEAPEST (a:Account COST 1)-[e:Transfers COST e.amount]->(b:Account) RETURN COUNT(*) AS result)
=> error:
